clue.text: Drive in fish to marshland

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for drive is placed inside the fish's name

parts.note: the tuna is a large sea fish
Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street addresses

explanation.surface: Someone herds fish onto boggy ground, a strange piece of angling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a verb, but it is the street-name abbreviation DR, which goes inside TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is treeless Arctic plain whose ground turns boggy and waterlogged in summer, so it is loosely a kind of marsh.

clue.text: Silly to protect turkey, which is uncooperative

indicators.note: to protect means to wrap around, so the word for silly encloses the turkey letters

parts.note: soppy means foolishly sentimental, silly
TR is the international vehicle registration code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A foolish person shields a turkey and turns out to be awkward about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' reads as the bird, but it is the country Turkey, whose international car code is TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stroppy is bad-tempered and awkward, refusing to cooperate.

clue.text: Actor who portrayed a crocodile at 25

definitions.text: Actor who portrayed a crocodile at 25

parts.words: Actor who portrayed a crocodile at 25
parts.note: 25 is the answer to 25-down, a Scottish city; the clue points to the Australian star of the 1986 film named Crocodile plus that city

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a film star and his famous reptilian role.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 25-down supplies DUNDEE, completing the film title Crocodile Dundee, whose title role was played by this Australian actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian comedian took the title role, the bushman Mick Dundee, in Crocodile Dundee.

clue.text: Make fun of deer I'd butchered

indicators.note: butchered means cut up and mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a deer that I have slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butchered' rearranges the letters of DEER ID.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride someone is to ridicule or mock them.

clue.text: The man's lower back is covered with hairs

parts.note: the man's means belonging to him, his

indicators.note: back tells us the word for lower is read from right to left

parts.note: to dip is to lower something

explanation.surface: Some man's lower back turns out to be rather hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower back' looks like a part of the body, but 'lower' is a verb meaning drop, and 'back' turns that word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispid is a botanical and zoological term for bristly, rough with stiff hairs.

clue.text: Significant in the past

definitions.meaning: important, likely to be remembered, as with a momentous event
belonging to bygone times, as in the ... present or ... sites

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both momentous, worth recording in history, and belonging to history, from earlier times.

clue.text: The lady has a degree of fame as a queen

parts.note: the lady is referred to as she
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A woman with a university qualification becomes as famous as royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical Queen of Sheba visited Solomon; the definition says the name is famed for its queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient kingdom is remembered chiefly for its legendary ruler who visited Solomon in the Bible.

clue.text: Tried pin out, which was bold

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tested a pin and was daring to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of TRIED PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrepid person is fearless and daring.

clue.text: Large organisation tracked down — or not

definitions.text: Large organisation tracked down — or not

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a huge international organisation
tracked down means found by following, traced

explanation.surface: A big international body was finally found — or perhaps it never was.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: UN plus TRACED builds the word, and 'or not' turns 'tracked down' into its opposite, which is what the prefix UN does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never found is not tracked down, the negative of having been located.

clue.text: Agrees to advantages of including Newton

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the advantages word takes the Newton letter within it

parts.note: assets are useful qualities or advantages
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Someone consents to the benefits of bringing Isaac Newton on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' reads as the scientist, but it is the unit of force, symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to give consent or approval.

clue.text: Dribble, like last, sad marsupial left

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word sad

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial

explanation.surface: A slobbering animal described as being like the last, a sad kangaroo left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' only joins the definition to the wordplay; 'last' picks the D at the end of 'sad'.
explanation.definitionFit: To drool is to let saliva run from the mouth, to slobber.

clue.text: Set off into action, carrying one weight at a time

indicators.note: carrying means bearing within, so the action word holds the other letters

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a ton is a unit of weight
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A bomb is set going in a busy scene where someone lifts one weight at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts TONAT inside DEED (D + E + TONAT + E + D); 'at a' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a charge is to set it off, causing it to explode.

clue.text: See half of it — barely

indicators.note: half of signals taking the final three of the six letters of the word barely

explanation.surface: Asked to look at half of something, the speaker says there is barely anything there.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'see' is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire. 'See' looks like a verb meaning look.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's seat or diocese is called a see, and the cathedral city in the Fens is one.

clue.text: Lily and Michael, holding a coal-scuttle

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the presenter's surname goes around the scuttle word

parts.note: Michael Aspel is a veteran British television presenter, known for This Is Your Life
a hod is a coal scuttle as well as a builder's trough

explanation.surface: Lily and Michael are carrying a bucket of coal between them.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Aspel is a long-serving British TV presenter; his surname goes round HOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a plant of the lily family, the flower of the Elysian fields in Greek myth.

clue.text: I am to be (it's said) in charge of metric scheme

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: it's said tells us to take the sound of the word be rather than its spelling

parts.note: the word be sounds like the letter B

explanation.surface: Someone declaring 'I am to be in charge' of a measuring system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only joins; the sound of 'be' gives the letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic verse uses the iamb, a short then long syllable, as its metre.

clue.text: He flies through the air, antenna first

parts.note: an aerial is an antenna for radio or television
first abbreviates to 1ST, read here with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A trapeze artist soars overhead, with the antenna leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST and the numeral 1 is read as the letter I; it also tells the solver which piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerialist is an acrobat on the trapeze or high wire, performing high above the ground.

clue.text: Shell hitting vehicle going quickly

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means swiftly, at speed

explanation.surface: A shell strikes a car speeding along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitting' just joins the definition to the wordplay; 'Shell' looks like an explosive shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise, crab or similar creature.

clue.text: Likely to take small flat

definitions.meaning: inclined or liable to do something
the short form of apartment, an abbreviated home

explanation.definitionFit: The word means inclined to, and it is also the written abbreviation for an apartment, a flat.

clue.text: Clear that it's el cid, plus unfinished work

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a new arrangement
unfinished means the word plus loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A claim that the legendary Spanish hero plus some incomplete job make things plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' trims PLUS to PLU; 'work' rearranges ELCID + PLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellucid water or prose is transparently clear.

clue.text: One fighter pilot

definitions.meaning: a single point, as the one on a playing card or die
an airman with many kills to his credit

explanation.definitionFit: The playing card counts as one, and a pilot who downs many enemy aircraft is also called by this name.

clue.text: Mainly a soldier

parts.note: read 'Mainly' as 'of the main', the old poetic word for the sea, so this is a seagoing soldier

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is chiefly a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' seems to mean chiefly, but the main is the sea, so a soldier of the main serves at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier trained to serve on ships and land from the sea.

clue.text: It's mined, partly for emeralds

indicators.note: partly means only part of the words for emeralds is used, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Something dug out of the ground, some of it valuable gemstones.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'fOR Emeralds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock from which metal is extracted, dug out in mines.

clue.text: Produces alcohol — but slipped up in one way

indicators.note: in signals that one group of letters is put within another
up, in a down clue, means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: slid means slipped
I is the Roman numeral for one
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A distiller makes spirits but takes a tumble along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SLID into DILS, and 'in' joins it with I and ST to give D(IST)ILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilling is how spirits are made, by boiling off and condensing the alcohol.

clue.text: Confirmed, on condition I charged round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the charged word goes about the other letters

parts.note: rated means charged, assessed for a fee
if means on condition that

explanation.surface: A deal is approved, provided that I paid around the going rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' means priced, not electrified or accused; 'round' wraps it around the condition word plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify an agreement is to formally approve or confirm it.

clue.text: A waste of snow

parts.note: sounds like a complaint about squandering snow, but a waste is also a desolate expanse

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the snow has been squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waste' reads as squandering, but it means a barren tract, here the polar region.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar region around the North Pole is a vast frozen wilderness of ice.

clue.text: Scottish city's dirty grey river

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: A Scottish city has a murky grey river running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dundee is a city on the Firth of Tay in eastern Scotland.

clue.text: A small magazine on the stand, and nothing long in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the stand word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a bier is a stand on which a coffin rests
taken as written
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A small magazine sits on a stand with nothing lengthy inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' looks like a publication but is a store of ammunition; the stand is the frame for a coffin, and 'in it' puts the other pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a shoulder belt with pockets for cartridges, a portable store of ammunition.

clue.text: Artist Rex is oddly rude to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the rearranged piece comes at the front
oddly means in an odd, irregular way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for Rex, king, as in royal cyphers

explanation.surface: An artist called Rex behaves strangely rudely at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' scrambles the clue's 'rude', and 'to begin with' sets that scramble ahead of the king's letter. Albrecht Dürer was the German Renaissance painter and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and printmaker.

clue.text: The French for "can meet up in Parisian quarter"

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A French phrase offered as the term for a rendezvous in a district of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin Quarter is the student district of Paris on the Left Bank; 'meet up in' just joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank student district is the Quartier Latin, named for the scholarly tongue once spoken there.

clue.text: Scoff at soldier's accommodation

definitions.meaning: to jeer at or heckle, as a crowd does a poor performer
a building housing troops, usually in the plural

explanation.definitionFit: To jeer loudly at players is to barrack them, and a building where troops are housed is a barrack.

clue.text: Norfolk town one might love will fade away

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, in the east of England

indicators.note: might suggests the letters could be otherwise arranged

explanation.surface: A Norfolk town that one might love is going to wither away.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, England; 'might' rearranges LOVE as OLVE; 'one' and 'will' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve is to melt or fade away into nothing.

clue.text: Was scared to admit the possibility of being deafer

indicators.note: the possibility of being suggests the letters could be turned into a different word

explanation.surface: Someone was afraid to confess that they might be going deaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the possibility of being' rearranges DEAFER; 'to admit' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been afraid of something is to have dreaded it.
